title: Can You Use a Stone to Mark Your Ball?
question: Your ball is on the putting green. You do not have a coin or a ball marker, so you place a small stone behind your ball before lifting it. Is this allowed?

choices.text: Yes. Any small object can be used to mark a ball.
Yes, as long as the stone does not move.
No. A stone is a natural object and is not a permitted ball-marker.
No. You must use a coin.

explanation: Before lifting a ball on the putting green, you must mark its spot by placing a ball-marker (an artificial object, such as a coin or purpose-made marker) immediately behind or next to the ball, or by holding a club on the ground immediately behind or next to the ball. A stone is a natural object, so it is not a ball-marker under the Rules. Many golfers think any small object will do, but the Rules specifically define a ball-marker as an artificial object.

juniorVersion.title: Can You Use a Stone to Show Where Your Ball Was?
juniorVersion.question: Your ball is on the putting green. You want to pick up your ball, but you don’t have a coin or a ball marker. You put a little stone behind your ball before you pick it up. Is this okay?

choices.text: Yes. You can use any small thing to mark your ball.
Yes, if the stone does not roll away.
No. You cannot use a stone because it is not a ball marker.
No. You must always use a coin.

juniorVersion.explanation: When you want to pick up your ball on the green, you must use a ball marker. A ball marker is a man-made thing, like a coin or a round marker from your pocket. A stone comes from the ground, so it does not count as a ball marker in golf.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The short, smooth grass near the hole where you putt the ball.
A small, man-made thing like a coin you use to show where your ball was.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show different objects and ask children which ones could be ball markers and which cannot, guiding them to spot the man-made markers.
likelyMisconceptions: Any small thing like a twig, stone, or leaf can be used to mark the ball.
You must always use a coin and nothing else.
